title: Financial Performance Comparison
description: Compare financial indicators between the main company and its competitors to evaluate performance and investment trends.
prompt_template: Analyze the financial performance of {{main_company}} and its main competitors in the {{industry}} sector. Compare key metrics such as revenue, profit margin, free cash flow, and capital investments. Highlight leaders, laggards, and patterns in financial health across competitors.
output_format:
Return ONLY a valid JSON array with the following schema: [ { "type_of_chart": "Bar", "chart_data": [ { "competitor": "string", ... } ] } ]. The structure of 'chart_data' depends on whether the bar chart is individual or grouped:

- **Individual bars**: Each object in 'chart_data' must have a 'competitor' (string, for the x-axis label) and a single 'value' (number, for the bar height). Example: [ { "type_of_chart": "Bar", "chart_data": [ { "competitor": "Microsoft", "value": 210 }, { "competitor": "Google", "value": 180 }, { "competitor": "Apple", "value": 250 } ] } ]. Use in Nivo: <ResponsiveBar data={chart_data} indexBy="competitor" keys={["value"]} />.

- **Grouped bars**: Each object in 'chart_data' must have a 'competitor' (string, for the x-axis label) and multiple numeric keys (e.g., 'revenue', 'profit_margin') for each bar group. Example: [ { "type_of_chart": "Bar", "chart_data": [ { "competitor": "Microsoft", "revenue": 210, "profit_margin": 30 }, { "competitor": "Google", "revenue": 180, "profit_margin": 25 }, { "competitor": "Apple", "revenue": 250, "profit_margin": 35 } ] } ]. Use in Nivo: <ResponsiveBar data={chart_data} indexBy="competitor" keys={["revenue", "profit_margin"]} groupMode="grouped" />.

If 'additional_information:' is provided, include it as a key named 'additional_information' with the text as a string.

variables.industry: Enter the industry or market sector (e.g., Software Services).

prompt_template: Compare {{main_company}} with its main competitors in the {{industry}} sector regarding innovation and sustainability. Evaluate R&D investments, patent activity, technology adoption, and environmental or social initiatives. Identify which competitors lead in innovation and which lag behind.
output_format: Return ONLY a valid JSON array with the following schema: [ { "type_of_chart": "Radar", "chart_data": [ { "competitor": "string", "dimension": "string (e.g., 'R&D', 'Innovation', 'Sustainability')", "value": number (score, positive number) } ] } ]. Example structure: [ { "type_of_chart": "Radar", "chart_data": [ { "competitor": "Siemens", "dimension": "R&D", "value": 80 }, { "competitor": "Siemens", "dimension": "Innovation", "value": 75 }, { "competitor": "Siemens", "dimension": "Sustainability", "value": 60 }, { "competitor": "GE", "dimension": "R&D", "value": 70 }, { "competitor": "GE", "dimension": "Innovation", "value": 65 }, { "competitor": "GE", "dimension": "Sustainability", "value": 55 } ] } ]. If 'additional_information:' is provided, include it as a key named 'additional_information' with the text as a string. For Nivo Radar: Use <ResponsiveRadar data={chart_data} keys={['Siemens', 'GE', ...]} indexBy="dimension" /> where 'keys' lists unique competitors, and 'dimension' defines the radar axes.

variables.main_company: Enter the main company name (e.g., Siemens).
variables.industry: Enter the industry or market sector (e.g., Industrial Technology).

title: Strategic Documents and Partnerships Analysis
description: Extract and summarize relationships, partnerships, and regulatory documents influencing competitiveness.
prompt_template: Using generative AI-driven document analysis, summarize key insights from environmental permits, contracts, government filings, and partnerships related to {{main_company}} and its competitors in the {{industry}} sector. Identify trends in alliances, projects, and collaborations impacting competitiveness.
output_format: Return ONLY a valid JSON array with the following schema: [ { "type_of_chart": "ScatterPlot", "chart_data": [ { "id": "string (entity or project name)", "x": number (investment or project scale), "y": number (impact or benefit level), "size": number (duration or relevance, positive number) } ] } ]. Example structure: [ { "type_of_chart": "ScatterPlot", "chart_data": [ { "id": "Partnership A", "x": 60, "y": 85, "size": 25 }, { "id": "Project B", "x": 40, "y": 70, "size": 15 } ] } ]. If 'additional_information:' is provided, include it as a key named 'additional_information' with the text as a string. For Nivo ScatterPlot: Use <ResponsiveScatterPlot data={[{ id: 'group', data: chart_data }]} /> where 'chart_data' is mapped as points with 'x', 'y', and 'size'.

variables.main_company: Enter the main company name (e.g., Shell).
variables.industry: Enter the industry or market sector (e.g., Energy and Petrochemicals).

title: Customer and Market Segment Insights
description: Analyze customer segments targeted by competitors to identify positioning opportunities and underserved markets.
prompt_template: Analyze the customer base and market segments targeted by {{main_company}} and its competitors in the {{industry}} sector. Identify customer demographics, segments served, and focus levels per company. Highlight emerging or underpenetrated segments that {{main_company}} could pursue.
output_format: Return ONLY a valid JSON array with the following schema: [ { "type_of_chart": "Sunburst", "chart_data": { "name": "string (root name, e.g., 'Market Segments')", "children": [ { "name": "string (segment)", "value": number (importance or percentage, positive number) }, { "name": "string (segment)", "children": [ { "name": "string (subsegment)", "value": number (importance or percentage, positive number) } ] } ] } } ]. Example structure: [ { "type_of_chart": "Sunburst", "chart_data": { "name": "Market Segments", "children": [ { "name": "Retail", "value": 40 }, { "name": "Enterprise", "children": [ { "name": "Finance", "value": 20 }, { "name": "Healthcare", "value": 15 } ] } ] } } ]. If 'additional_information:' is provided, include it as a key named 'additional_information' with the text as a string. For Nivo Sunburst: Use <ResponsiveSunburst data={chart_data} /> where 'children' defines hierarchical segments, and 'value' determines segment size.

variables.main_company: Enter the main company name (e.g., Amazon).
variables.industry: Enter the industry or market sector (e.g., E-commerce).
